title: How to dance The Charleston from the 1920s

method.teacher_system: The teacher breaks down the Charleston into small, manageable components, starting with the basic footwork without twists. She then introduces the twists and weight shifts, layering these elements together. Finally, she demonstrates the full step at a faster, more authentic tempo.
method.signature: The teacher explicitly separates the footwork from the twists, allowing learners to master the basic rhythm before adding the characteristic style.

practices.what: The teacher demonstrates the basic Charleston step without the twists to establish the rhythm.
The teacher isolates the timing of the twists, showing how they fit into the basic step.
The teacher guides the learner through shifting weight from one foot to the other while incorporating the twists.
The teacher combines all the previously learned components into the full, fluid Charleston step.

moments.says: The teacher introduces the Charleston by demonstrating the basic step without twists.
The teacher explains the weight distribution and the movement of the heels before adding the twists.
The teacher encourages the learner to practice shifting their weight from one foot to the other while incorporating the twists.
The teacher notes that the step is usually danced a little faster and demonstrates the increased tempo.
The teacher invites the learner to join weekly classes to learn more authentic vintage jazz steps.

mentor.what_stays: The teacher leaves the learner feeling capable of mastering the Charleston by breaking it down into manageable, progressive steps.

struggles.theme: feeling uncoordinated or having two left feet
dance looks easy but is actually difficult

method.limits: The video does not include audio of the music, only the teacher's counts, so the musicality and groove are not fully demonstrated.
